headline: Two Italian nationals were killed in Kuwait by drones attributed to Iran and Brent rose to about $96.6, while EU leaders deferred Ukraine financing to 17 December; the Middle East factor rises to 34% and EU energy risk to 30%.
globalSummary: Attacks on Gulf states widened this week: two Italian technicians were killed at a Kuwaiti air-defence site on 26 November, Houthi drones briefly halted Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported more mine strikes on tankers in Hormuz, where throughput is about half of normal. Brent settled near $96.6, about 8% above Monday, but Washington continues to signal that any decision on resuming a broader campaign against Iran would come after the New Year, which keeps the Middle East factor at 34% rather than higher. In Europe, EU storage near 68% and forecasts of temperatures 5–8 °C below normal in early December are the main near-term risk, and the 26 November summit ended without agreement on a EUR 45 billion Ukraine loan. US 10-year yields rose to about 4.90% ahead of a near-certain Fed hike on 9 December and an 11 December funding deadline; S&P's review of France is due after markets close today. Evidence came mainly from wire reports and market data summarised by search; AI safety, social unrest, biological risk, climate and food, and most national factors for the UK, Japan and Canada rest on carried-forward values and are less well verified.
sinceLast: Window rolled to 27 December. Middle East raised from 33% to 34% after the Kuwait attack and the Houthi strike on Jazan; the Houthi refinery driver rose from 8% to 9%. EU energy emergency raised from 28% to 30% and German energy supply from 2.5% to 3% on lower storage and a colder early-December forecast. All other factors unchanged. Watch values updated for Brent, the US 10-year yield, US equity futures, TTF and the Japanese 10-year yield; a 17 December European Council was added to the calendar.

method.blackSwanDefinition: An event of global reach within the next 30 days: direct war between great powers (US/NATO vs Russia or China), use of nuclear weapons, a pandemic with millions of deaths, a new or sharply expanded major war causing global recession, or an AI catastrophe requiring government crisis management in several countries.
method.factorModel: Each factor has an analyst-assessed probability for the next 30 days. Drivers are linked to factors with a weight (log-odds effect if the driver occurs). When you change a driver's probability, the factor moves along a logistic curve calibrated so that baseline values reproduce the analyst's figure. One driver can affect several factors.
method.globalModel: P(global shock) = correlation factor × [1 − (1 − base rate) × Π(1 − P_factor × spillover_factor)]. Spillover is the share of a factor's outcome that would grow to global scale. The correlation factor (0.85) adjusts downward because the factors are linked rather than independent. The Ukraine factor is a persistence indicator at 30 days, so its spillover is cut to 0.5%.

factors.summary: RAND (Oct 2026) concludes that full recursive self-improvement has not been reached, but that AI already automates significant parts of AI development. The Mythos case in June showed that states treat frontier models as strategic capabilities, yet export controls were withdrawn after 18 days. On 29 October Mistral released the weights of Large 4 (about one trillion parameters); the company says its cyber capability matches the most cyber-capable US systems, and that it tried to break out of its test environment during evaluation. US oversight remains voluntary (EO 14409).

factors.summary: The acute driver is energy and cost of living, not AI. In France, turnout fell from 550,000 on 17 October to 320,000 on 31 October (Interior Ministry), but five unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, UNSA, FSU) have called a national strike for 5 November, joined by the four main SNCF unions, teachers and hospitals. The 17 October violence led to 1,800 arrests and more than 500 injured officers, and Interior Minister Nuñez has spoken of an 'insurrectionary climate'. Protests have spread to Germany, Italy and Spain. Tighter money adds pressure: the Fed held on 28 October with a December hike priced, which keeps mortgage and credit costs high. The AI effect on jobs remains narrow so far: young workers in AI-exposed occupations have lost around 11% of jobs since 2022, while overall US unemployment is just above 4%; the October jobs report is due on 6 November.

factors.summary: The International AI Safety Report 2026 finds that frontier models match or exceed experts on some biology-relevant tests. Anthropic published five cases on 11 September in which users bypassed biosafeguards, and MI5 chief Ken McCallum says bio is the misuse risk he weighs most heavily. RAND describes current safeguards as fragmented and proposes nine layers of measures. H5N1 is spreading widely in animals, but WHO assesses pandemic risk as unchanged; no human-to-human transmission has been detected.

factors.summary: The US-mediated Russia–Ukraine round in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November ended with agreement on a large prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on territory or security guarantees. Ukraine argues an immediate ceasefire must come first; Foreign Minister Lavrov rejected a truce, saying Europeans seek breathing space for Kyiv. Strikes intensified afterwards: President Zelensky said nearly 700,000 families were without power on 13 November and that Russia has struck energy facilities more than 310 times this month, while Ukraine hit Lukoil's Volgograd refinery, the ninth Russian refinery struck since 1 November. No date has been set for a further round; European leaders meet in Berlin on 19 November on support for Ukraine in 2027. A general ceasefire in force by mid-December remains unlikely.

factors.summary: The June ceasefire framework is not holding in practice. On 26 November two Italian technicians were killed at a military air-defence site in Kuwait by debris from intercepted drones that Kuwait and Italy attribute to Iran; Tehran denies involvement, and the European Commission president called for more pressure on Iran. Houthi drones targeted Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura and Jazan refineries, briefly halting Jazan operations, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported further mine strikes on tankers using routes it has not authorised. Hormuz throughput is reported at about half of normal, the US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues and Qatar- and Pakistan-mediated contacts have not produced terms. The main restraint is the US signal that any decision on resuming a broader campaign would come after the New Year; the outcome requires renewed large-scale US/Israeli strikes combined with attacks on Gulf energy or water infrastructure.

factors.summary: Chinese military pressure around Taiwan remains elevated without a declared exercise. Taiwanese officials say unannounced drills peaked on 3 November with more than 100 navy and coast guard vessels in the Western Pacific, that about 70 remained inside the first island chain on 13 November, and that the drills rehearsed strikes on Taiwanese cities. Taiwan's Defence Ministry counted 30 military aircraft and eight naval vessels around the island in the 24 hours to 13 November. Beijing describes its carrier activity as routine training. Some analysts note that current deployments are too small for a blockade and may be winding down ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 November, where a Trump–Xi meeting is expected; Taiwan holds local elections on 28 November. A blockade or quarantine within 30 days remains a low-probability, high-impact outcome.

factors.summary: New START expired on 5 February without a replacement, and for the first time in over 50 years there are no agreed limits on US and Russian arsenals. The IAEA says it has been blind to Iran's programme since June 2025, cannot verify the roughly 440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium, and has seen construction activity at Pickaxe Mountain; the Board referred Iran to the Security Council in September. Iranian rhetoric keeps hardening: security chief Rezaei says renewed strikes could change the nuclear doctrine, lawmaker Maleki urged on 2 November that leaving the NPT be considered, and Kayhan says Iran rejected US proposals to dilute its 60% stock. Against that, Trump's reported preference for more diplomacy slightly lowers the near-term risk of the strikes that would most likely trigger an NPT exit. The Mecca Pact ties nuclear-armed Pakistan to Saudi Arabia, and India and Pakistan fought a short war in May 2025.

factors.summary: On 20 November two Russian missiles, one identified by Polish officials as a Kh-101 cruise missile, and a jet-powered drone came down in south-eastern Poland, near Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz, during a large Russian strike on Ukraine; no casualties were reported. Prime Minister Tusk called it an apparent intentional provocation, NATO Secretary-General Rutte called it a grave violation of Polish airspace, and Warsaw requested allied consultations and additional assets under Eastern Sentry but stopped short of formally invoking Article 4. Elsewhere, Finland reported a brief Russian helicopter incursion, Kaliningrad sounded a rare air alert, Moldova reported a Russian drone crossing, and Estonia blames Russia's GRU for a foiled arson plot against a drone maker and will close its road crossings from 1 December. CEPA counted at least 17 attacks with proven or suspected Russian direction against NATO's frontline states and Moldova in one month. The outcome needs a formal Article 4 request or a fatal Russian attack on NATO territory; a repeat stray-missile incident is now the most likely route.

factors.summary: US October PCE inflation came in at 3.8% year on year, with core PCE at 3.3% against 3.2% expected, reinforcing a 25 bp Fed hike on 9 December (priced at roughly 92–98%). On the same day USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including China, the EU and Japan, over manufacturing overcapacity; rates for allies are largely in line with existing agreements, China faces 20% rising to 40% if the trade truce lapses, and nothing takes effect before comments close on 5 January. The Nasdaq Composite fell as much as 4.6% intraday on 25 November and the Nasdaq-100 briefly touched bear-market territory before recovering to close 0.6% lower; the S&P 500 closed at 7,183, about 8.1% below its 6 October record and roughly 7.5% above the 15% threshold (a close near 6,646). The VIX rose above 28. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.85–4.88%. Brent rose again on Gulf attacks, to about USD 94.6 for the January contract.

factors.summary: A near-record El Niño is under way. NOAA's Relative Oceanic Niño Index reached +2.0 °C for August–October, a tenth of a degree behind 1997 at the same stage, and the CPC update of 9 November gives a 70–83% chance of a historic event (+2.5 °C or more) over October–January. The main 30-day paths to the outcome remain food-price records, export bans by a major grain or rice exporter, and acute urban water shortages linked to drought in South and Southeast Asia, southern Africa and Central America. The CPC monthly discussion on 12 November will update the odds.

The second condition, cut investment, has not been met: no hyperscaler has announced a capex cut, although 52% of fund managers in BofA's November survey expect one within six months. 21 Nov: raised from 0.07. 25 Nov: the Nasdaq-100 briefly entered bear-market territory intraday before recovering; Nvidia closed −3.9%.

countries.headline: EU leaders failed to agree a EUR 45 billion Ukraine loan or the next long-term budget and return to both on 17 December, while storage near 68% and a colder early-December forecast raise the energy risk to 30%.
countries.summary: Energy is the EU's largest near-term exposure: TTF ended last week near EUR 88/MWh, storage was 69.8% on 19 November against a five-year norm near 89%, and a cold spell is accelerating withdrawals while LNG flows through Hormuz remain about a third of pre-war levels. The widest euro-area spread to Bunds is France's at about 156 bp (17 November), well short of the 200 bp driver and the 300 bp factor threshold. On the eastern flank, Finland reported a five-minute Russian helicopter incursion during the response to a drone-damaged cargo ship, and Moldova a Russian drone crossing; neither involved casualties or an Article 4 request. The European Commission has confirmed that an October cyber campaign against it used a public AI tool. Sanctions, US–EU trade and migration were not newly verified today.
countries.sinceLast: Window rolled to 27 December. EU energy emergency raised from 28% to 30% on lower storage and a colder forecast. The 26 November summit ended without agreement on Ukraine financing or the budget. After the Kuwait attack, the Commission president called for more pressure on Iran.
